mechanism: Amphotericin B causes nephrotoxicity and renal tubular dysfunction, impairing the conversion of 25-hydroxyvitamin D to active 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D in the kidneys, leading to vitamin D deficiency and hypocalcemia.
action: Monitor serum calcium, phosphate, and vitamin D levels regularly during amphotericin B therapy; consider vitamin D supplementation if deficiency develops and renal function permits.
